judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: No-claim row. The element is the only content of the image link to /paint-decorating/decorating-tools in the category grid (photo of a brush, roller and colour fan), with alt "Visit our Decorating Tools category"; the snapshot's AX tree gives the link that name. Under 1.1.1 Situation C (H30) and the G82 test, the alternative must state the control's purpose: it names the destination, and the destination page's h1 is "Decorating Tools", so the alternative describes the link's function and the image meets 1.1.1. I looked for reasons it could still fail (an empty or file-name alt, a crop or name the collector got wrong, a different live version) and found none. A sighted user also has the visible h3 "Decorating Tools" under the image, so nothing is lost. captureDiffers: the screenshot is fully styled, and the live HTML fetched on 2026-11-21 has the same anchor, href and alt; my fetch is automated too, but nothing suggests a bot-only version.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: No-claim row. The element is the main-navigation link with visible text "Bathroom & Plumbing", aria-label "Go to Bathroom & Plumbing" and href /bathroom-plumbing. Its destination's title and heading are "Bathroom & Plumbing", so the link text alone gives its purpose (2.4.4 met; ARIA8). The aria-label holds the visible text, so there is no mismatch, and aria-expanded only adds that it opens a submenu. No other link in the snapshot has the same accessible name, so the shared-name test (R1) does not apply; the submenu's "Shop All Bathroom & Plumbing" link has another name and goes to the same page anyway. captureDiffers: the screenshot shows the styled nav bar with this item, and the live HTML fetched on 2026-11-21 has identical markup for the anchor.
